title: Choose the visual world for the Case IQ landing page (new hand)
question: The roll assigned The Fact-Checker's Galley. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Fact-Checker's Galley
options.lineage: copy editors' blue-pencil checks on galley proofs, and the teacher's tick in the margin
options.thesis: Every line of your story, checked against your papers: ticked where they show it, flagged where they don't.
materials: white galley strips with numbered lines
options.viewport: A galley strip of your story lies on a green cutting mat; blue-pencil ticks check each line, margin notes give the page it came from, one line is flagged 'Source?', and the only clean, unmarked panel holds the first step of getting help.
options.risk: Newsroom craft can drift toward the broadsheet-editorial look, and few people know galley proofs, so the familiar teacher's tick and the pencil hand must carry it.

raised.raise: Certainty is drawn, not coloured: a fact stated in a document gets a solid mark, a computer-read one a dashed mark, and a missing one an empty outline.
One line grid governs the page: galley lines are numbered and every margin check sits on the line it checks.
One fact per row, with its locator stamped in the margin beside it.
Every fact carries the same three-band label: when, what, and where it's written.
The action lives in the page's one calm, unmarked panel.
One action colour, used only on things you can press.

options.label: The Phone Roll
options.lineage: chat threads, screenshots and the camera roll where most people's evidence lives
options.thesis: Your case already lives in your phone; we turn the chats and screenshots into a timeline with pages.
options.viewport: A long chat thread fills the screen; one bubble lifts off with its date and page pinned to it, and the reply bar becomes the primary action.
options.risk: The most familiar idea of this hand: it can look like a messaging app or a competitor's app page, and can make a court case feel trivial.

options.label: Collider Event Display
options.thesis: Your case as one frozen event with tracks radiating out.
options.viewport: Concentric rings with each paper as a track curving out from the centre.
options.case: Fuses poorly: visitors don't recognize it, and it makes the case look like a physics problem.
options.kept: Certainty drawn as line style, not colour.
options.risk: Cold, technical and dark, which is the opposite of calm.

options.label: ASCII Scene
options.thesis: Your papers rendered as living text characters.
options.viewport: A scene drawn in characters that resolves into your timeline.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it reads as hacking, and hides the human help.
options.kept: One strict line grid for the whole page.
options.risk: Inaccessible and alienating for stressed visitors.

options.label: Hand-Processed Film
options.thesis: Your story as frames on a strip, each one numbered.
options.viewport: A film strip with each event as a frame and its source on the edge code.
options.case: Fuses for sequence, but the scratches and light leaks fight the message that nothing is distorted.
options.kept: One fact per row, with its locator stamped in the margin.
options.risk: Moody and nostalgic, and damage effects suggest altered evidence.

options.label: Pickling Calendar
options.thesis: Your case sorted onto a shelf by month, every jar labelled.
options.viewport: A shelf of labelled jars, one per month of your case.
options.case: Fuses for dated labels, but trivializes a court case.
options.kept: One label anatomy for every fact: when, what, where.

options.label: Festival Flyer
options.thesis: A loud collage with one calm white panel.
options.viewport: A full-bleed collage with the intake floating in one white panel.
options.case: Fuses poorly: party energy is the wrong tone for someone facing a hearing.
options.kept: The action lives in the one calm panel.
options.risk: Overwhelming and flippant for this audience.

options.label: Punk Paste-Up Zine
options.viewport: A stapled zine spread with ransom-letter headlines.
options.case: Fuses poorly: ransom-note lettering reads as a threat.
options.kept: A single action colour reserved for what you can press.
options.risk: Hostile and chaotic for stressed visitors.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What consumer legal-help sites ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and button on the left, a timeline screenshot on the right, and a trust row below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other legal-tech sites by design.
